findings.quote: the envoys sent to arrange a settlement joined the envoys from Greece
findings.problem: Greek: συνῆψαν τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἑλλάδος πρεσβευτῶν οἱ πεμφθέντες ἐπὶ τὰς διαλύσεις. The genitive is partitive: 'those of the envoys from Greece who had been sent to arrange a settlement' are the subject (verb συνάπτω, 'met/came up'). English invents two separate groups of envoys; the following speakers (Achaeans, Athenians, Eudemus of Miletus) are all the Greek envoys.
findings.proposed_fix: those of the envoys from Greece who had been sent to arrange a settlement came to meet him

findings.problem: Greek: τὴν συγγένειαν καὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν τὴν τοῦ Πτολεμαίου. Both kinship and youth belong to Ptolemy; 'the king' after 'Antiochus' reads as Antiochus.

units.note: Remainder (Naucratis, gold coin, Aristides and Theris, dowry agreement with Antiochus III) accurate.
150 talents / 50 for a crown (στέφανον) to Rome correct.
